text:
Elaine: Heads-up — I'm drafting a short proposal for a single-dashboard view that covers Hosted + Dedicated GPU pools. Need SM occupancy, per-SM memory, queue depth by priority, and routing/quota signals. Any objections to combining pools into one pane?
Kartik: +1 for unified view. Question: do we have stable metric names across runtime and infra today?
Maya: Not yet. Runtime currently emits `sm_occupancy` per gpu_id; infra has `pool_level_utilization`. We should agree on a consumer contract.
Jin: Can we include `model_variant` and `capacity_tier` labels? That makes routing-policy traces way easier.
Elaine: Yes — add `model_variant` + `capacity_tier`. Also want `request_queue_depth` with a `queue_priority` label (regular/priority/burst).
Kartik: Proposal for canonical names/labels:
```
sm_occupancy{pool, gpu_id, capacity_tier, model_variant}
sm_memory_used_bytes{pool, gpu_id, capacity_tier}
sm_queue_depth{pool, queue_priority}
served_request_total{pool, model_variant, route_reason}
quota_utilization_by_customer{pool, customer_bucket, capacity_tier}
```
Maya: runtime note — `sm_occupancy` is sampled per-second. `sm_memory_used_bytes` is a point-in-time gauge per allocation. For queue depth we can export either a gauge or a histogram. Which do we want?
Jin: gauge for depth, histogram for wait latency. Alerts should use gauge + rate of change.
Elaine: ConsoleTeam: we need aggregated rollups: pool-level percentiles, p95 queue depth, and headroom_by_pool. Also breakdown by customer tier for Dedicated.
ConsoleTeam: We prefer pre-aggregated series (server-side rollups) to avoid heavy client-side compute. Ideally an API like `/api/metrics/v1/pools/{pool}/rollups?window=1m&agg=p95`.
InfraBot: infra-ci: exported metrics must keep cardinality budgets in mind (target <30k series per cluster). Tagging by `gpu_id` is OK for troubleshooting but rollups should be the default.
Maya: runtime can emit both `per_gpu` and `pool_rollup` metrics. `pool_rollup` reduces cardinality and is cheap to ingest.
Kartik: Also want routing decision visibility. Add `route_reason` on `served_request_total` (values: `latency`, `cost`, `fallback`, `overprovision`). Helps correlate spikes to fallback behavior.
Jin: SLO/Oncall request — support drilling into canary vs stable. Add `rollout_tag` label (canary/stable).
Elaine: Good — add `rollout_tag`. Also include metadata labels: `export_version` and `sample_rate` for compatibility.
Maya: Ops question: how do Dedicated quotas show up? `quota_utilization_by_customer{customer_bucket, pool, capacity_tier}` maybe?
Kartik: Don't expose raw `customer_id` in dashboards (PII). Use `customer_bucket` or a hashed `org_id`.
ConsoleTeam: Agreed — hashed org id only. We can accept `customer_bucket` for dashboard grouping. We'll also need an endpoint to request rollup windows.
Jin: Sample relabel snippet for promtail/prometheus relabeling:
```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_k8s_pod_label_pool]
    target_label: pool
  - source_labels: [__meta_k8s_pod_label_model_variant]
    target_label: model_variant
```
Elaine: Timeline check — runtime PR for metric renames in 2 weeks? Console needs rollups live in 4 weeks for Hosted->Dedicated rollout. Is that feasible?
Maya: Tight but doable. I'll spike this afternoon and aim for a proto PR by EOD.
Kartik: I'll draft the infra consumer contract and a cardinality budget doc this week.
ConsoleTeam: We'll mock the UI with sample data and post in #design for feedback.
Jin: Alert proposals: `queue_depth > 200 for 5m` OR `sm_occupancy > 95%` with low headroom -> page oncall.
Elaine: Thanks — I'll consolidate notes into a short design doc and link here. @Maya ping me when the PR is up. :seedling:
InfraBot: infra-ci: created ticket INF-4321 for metric-rollout coordination (assigned to Maya/Kartik).
